title: Goodly Trials Stats Explained
summary: Read vitals, attributes, and combat values without treating a single number as the whole unit.
quickAnswer: HP, ES, and MP describe resources; STR, AGI, and INT are attributes; ATK, CRT, RNG, SPD, AR, and EVA describe combat behavior.

sections.title: Vitals
paragraphs: HP is hit points; reaching zero removes the unit. ES absorbs damage before HP and regenerates. MP is spent to cast spell tomes in trinket slots.
bullets: HP — hit points and survival
ES — regenerating damage buffer
MP — spell resource

sections.title: Attributes
paragraphs: STR, AGI, and INT shape several derived values. A unit's primary attribute can also feed ATK and eventually support an Ascendancy choice.
bullets: STR — HP, armor, recovery, and ATK when primary
AGI — HP, speed, evasion, and ATK when primary
INT — MP, regeneration, ES, and ATK when primary

sections.title: Combat values
paragraphs: Combat values tell you how a unit deals, avoids, or reduces damage and where it can attack.
bullets: ATK — hit damage before AR, with a minimum of 1
CRT — chance to deal double damage
RNG — attack distance in tiles; 1 is melee
SPD — action and movement speed
AR — flat damage reduction
EVA — chance to avoid before AR or ES

title: Goodly Trials Formation Guide
summary: Use range, adjacency, tactics, and the opposing line to decide where a recruit belongs before combat begins.
quickAnswer: Formation is not only front versus back. Read each unit's tactic, range, adjacency effects, and equipment before locking the line.

sections.title: Read the tactic first
paragraphs: The current public unit sample exposes three tactic labels: Formation, Backline, and Flanking. They describe behavior after the line breaks and should be read before any generic role label.
bullets: Formation — stays in formation and can reduce damage taken
Backline — prefers to stay behind the line
Flanking — can enter from behind enemy lines

sections.title: Protect adjacency value
paragraphs: Some skills and traits affect adjacent allies. A Goodly Knight adds STR to adjacent allies, while a Skeleton Child transfers part of hand-gear benefits to adjacent allies. Repositioning can therefore change the value of the same shop purchase.
bullets: Check every adjacent-effect sentence
Confirm the unit still has a useful target
Avoid breaking a support pair for an unverified role assumption

sections.title: Commit with the enemy line in mind
paragraphs: Goodly Trials resolves combat automatically after placement. The official description emphasizes range, formation, flanking, adjacency, and the shape of the opposing line. Inspect first; commit second.

title: Goodly Trials Flanking Explained
summary: Flanking units can enter behind enemy lines, but their value still depends on the opposing board and survivability.
quickAnswer: A Flanking tactic creates a rear-entry possibility; it does not guarantee a safe target or a successful kill.

sections.title: What the public cards confirm
paragraphs: Skeleton Child and Skeleton Dog both carry the Flanking tactic in the current public unit sample. The official wording says they can enter combat from behind enemy lines.
bullets: Skeleton Child also has a once-per-battle back-corner respawn
Skeleton Dog gains value when allies die through Feast
Neither card guarantees which enemy will be reached first

sections.title: Pre-combat checks
paragraphs: Look at rear-space availability, enemy range, and whether your flanker can survive long enough for its trait or skill to matter.
bullets: Identify exposed backline targets
Check whether rear space is contested
Do not sacrifice the rest of the formation only to force a flank

title: Goodly Trials Game Modes
summary: Compare the single-player journey, Ranked climb, and 2–8 player tournament.
quickAnswer: Single-player and Ranked follow a twelve-trial road; multiplayer uses live bidding, preparation, combat, and season standings for 2–8 companies.

sections.title: Single-player road
paragraphs: Training leads to Fair Trial, then Unfair Trial and Ranked. Three battles without a win end a journey. Completing roads unlocks later challenges and progression systems.
bullets: Twelve trials
Three battles without a win end the journey
Fair unlocks bosses and Deed spending
Unfair unlocks Old Man and later leader traits

sections.title: Ranked ladder
paragraphs: The current official modes page is internally inconsistent: its prose says Ranked begins at Soldier: 200, while the threshold list says Soldier: 100. This archive records both statements and does not choose a value without further official or in-game confirmation.
bullets: Unresolved source conflict — Soldier is 200 in prose and 100 in the list
Peasant — 0
Soldier — 100 (threshold list)
Squire — 300
Knight — 500
Veteran — 700
Marshal — 900
High Marshal — 1,150
Champion — 1,400

sections.title: Multiplayer tournament
paragraphs: A host seats humans and AI and chooses how often companies meet. Players bid in a shared market, lock their lines, fight the table, and follow standings until a champion remains.
bullets: 2–8 companies
Live bidding for contested items
Mixed-faction lobbies can also auction units
AI armies can fill empty seats
